questions.ask: Run agent-config-kit's backend quality gate on every pull request (.github/workflows/quality-gate.yml)?
questions.why: Installs a small caller of the kit's be-hono-quality-gate workflow, pinned to one commit: format, lint, types, tests with coverage, migration drift, index coverage, runtime hardening and secret scans, with a read-only token and no secrets. It needs GitHub Actions; an existing quality-gate.yml is kept either way.
questions.detect: the repo is on GitHub (a github.com remote or a .github/ folder); .github/workflows/quality-gate.yml already exists

questions.ask: Review each pull request with DeepSeek, a low-cost paid AI model (.github/workflows/deepseek-review.yml)?
questions.why: Installs a caller of agent-config-kit's reusable DeepSeek review, with notes about this stack: one comment per pull request from a branch of this repository, updated when the repository's owner, a member or a collaborator comments /ask-deepseek. It reads the diff over the GitHub API and runs no pull-request code. It needs the repository secret DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and costs about ten US cents a review at most, usually a cent or two (the diff and the answer are capped); without the secret it passes and sends nothing.
questions.detect: .github/workflows/deepseek-review.yml already exists, or the user has asked for an AI review in CI

questions.ask: Add pull-request templates for work pull requests and dev → prod promotions (.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/)?
questions.why: They list only what the gate cannot decide: the schema and query checks a person reads, and the migration and deploy steps of a promotion. They assume dev and prod branches.
questions.detect: branches dev and prod exist (git branch --list dev prod); .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/ already has files

questions.ask: Does an agent need to read a self-hosted analytics API from this repo?
questions.why: Adds .claude/ANALYTICS.example.md, a template to fill in for that read API. An unfilled template is worse than none, because an agent will try to use it.
questions.detect: the code or .env.*.example names an analytics client, or .claude/ANALYTICS.md exists

questions.ask: Do you open several repositories as one Serena workspace?
questions.why: Adds .claude/SERENA-WORKSPACE.example.md, which explains how to scope Serena's searches across repos. With a single repo the default needs no documentation.
questions.detect: .mcp.json runs Serena and a .serena/project.yml above this repo lists several folders, or AGENT_WORKSPACE_ROOT is set

questions.ask: Seal request and response bodies between this API and its callers (the payload contract: encrypted envelopes, one endpoint registry, checked before merge)?
questions.why: Yes installs the payload contract: a reference implementation in src/lib/payload/ (AES-256-GCM envelopes bound to method, route and status; pre-shared key rings; browser key agreement; a Hono middleware; the strict/off switch) with its tests at 100%, the endpoint registry and its generator, check:endpoints (registry drift, route literals, reasons, the committed switch) and check:crypto-interop (the shared test vectors, and peers checked out beside this repo), the contract document and a rule that loads when you touch the middleware, the registry or payload.config.json. Wiring it into the app stays yours: the contract document shows where. No new dependency (WebCrypto). Answer no when bodies need no sealing beyond TLS.
questions.detect: payload.config.json or src/lib/payload/ already exists, or the frontends that call this API seal their bodies

packageScripts.fl: bun run format && bun run lint
packageScripts.fl:ci: bun run format:check && oxlint --type-aware src scripts
packageScripts.check:crypto-interop: if [ -f scripts/check/crypto-interop.ts ]; then bun scripts/check/crypto-interop.ts ; else echo 'check:crypto-interop skipped: setup did not install the payload module'; fi
packageScripts.check:endpoints: if [ -f scripts/check/endpoints.ts ]; then bun scripts/check/endpoints.ts ; else echo 'check:endpoints skipped: setup did not install the payload module'; fi
